A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GIST research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–J. The complete material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original GIST evaluations on MMLU, TYDIQA, and BBH, efficiency measurements, ablations, transfer experiments, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and the appendices, including benchmark comparisons, efficiency measurements, and ablations.

M1.justification: The warmup, spectral filtering, projected cosine scoring, maximum-relevance aggregation, and top-k selection procedure remain unchanged. Transposing the gradient matrix and replacing right singular vectors with left singular vectors preserves the same parameter-space projector.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same FLAN V2, COT, DOLLY, and OPEN ASSISTANT1 training pool and evaluate MMLU, TYDIQA, and BBH. The transfer scenarios and Telugu case study are also retained.

E2.justification: The reported comparisons retain Base, Full, Random, Length, PPL, Embedding, and RDS+, alongside LESS. Comparator participation in the appendix experiments is unchanged. Newly discussed related methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices G–I retain the model configurations, selection budgets, training schedules, projection ranks, evaluation metrics, and checkpoint-selection procedures. No experimental protocol is added or substantively revised.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same checkpoint and projection-rank sensitivity studies, spectral and training-dynamics analyses, cross-model transfer, warmup and LoRA-rank ablations, tail-direction experiment, and Telugu retrieval case study.

E5.justification: The three-trial reporting and standard deviations are unchanged. Appendix G.3 retains the same explanation of varying selection/warmup partitions while holding optimization seeds fixed; no uncertainty estimation procedure is added.

E6.justification: The numerical tables, plotted results, and qualitative retrieval examples are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains GIST's average improvements of +6.2, +4.5, and +1.5 for Llama2-7B, Llama3.2-3B, and Qwen2.5-1.5B, respectively.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.2 and Appendix E.2 replace the within-factor curvature statement with an explicit mixed A–B derivative and a new proof retaining the gradient-dependent bilinear term. This corrects v1's unjustified removal of that chain-rule contribution. Separately, Appendix J retains the old V-based Hessian formulas after the gradient matrix is transposed, introducing a dimensional inconsistency.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same geometric motivation, GIST contribution, and performance-efficiency claims, including 0.29% of baseline storage and 25% of computational time. The revised theorem supports the existing central claim.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 newly acknowledges that checkpoint aggregation can partly mitigate the limited expressivity of a single-checkpoint diagonal surrogate. This qualifies the comparison with optimizer-based approaches. Appendix A's substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Hardware, hyperparameters, preprocessing, runtime information, and code-access disclosures are retained. Section 5.5's explicit Gram-product notation restates the already documented target-sized Gram computation under the transposed matrix convention.

R1.justification: Appendix B substantially revises positioning by expanding attribution coverage to DataInf, multi-source fine-tuning, and influence-preserving proxies, and connecting GIST to GaLore, SOAP, and Muon. It replaces v1's blanket LESS/TRAK diagonal-approximation framing and paradigm-shift language with more differentiated comparisons and shared geometric principles.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and notation edits, rewrites related-work paragraphs, and adds acknowledgments and proceedings information. The overall section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is enlarged and visually revised while retaining the same pipeline. Caption styling, table spacing, and text placement change modestly. All eight figures and eleven tables remain, without new experimental displays.

improvement.justification: The revised Theorem 3.2 and Appendix E.2 repair the treatment of bilinear curvature and better support the central coupling argument; Appendix B also provides broader, more careful positioning. These gains outweigh a localized regression: Appendix J's retained Hessian formulas conflict with the transposed gradient convention. The net improvement is limited because that inconsistency remains, while the algorithm and empirical evidence are unchanged.
